Criminal proceeding initiated against the petitioners in Crime No.505/2021 of Madanayakanahally Police Station, Bengaluru District is sought to be quashed in this petition.

2. On the basis of a complaint lodged by respondent No.2, the aforementioned case was registered against her husband and parents-in-law for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
An application under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure is filed signed by the petitioners as well as respondent No.2, seeking permission of the Court to compound the matter.

4. It is stated that M.C.No.802/2023 filed by petitioner No.1 against respondent No.2 on the file of I Additional Senior Civil Judge, Bengaluru Rural District seeking divorce was referred to Mediation Centre, Bangalore and the matter got settled, wherein petitioner No.1 has agreed to pay Rs.4,75,000/- towards permanent alimony to respondent No.2.

sentences.text: 5. I have perused the order passed in M.C.No.802/2023, wherein the learned Judge has accepted the Memorandum of Settlement filed by the parties and closed the said case in view of the Mediation report.
As per Memorandum of Settlement, the balance of Rs.1,00,000/- was agreed to be paid by way of Demand Draft after quashing of the present petition.
7. The petitioners as well as respondent No.2 are present before the Court.

The Demand Draft bearing No.770372, dated 27.02.2025 for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- drawn in favour of respondent No.2-Kruthika, has been handed over to respondent No.2.
8.

In B.S.Joshi and Ors. vs State of Harayana and Anr.1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that it becomes the duty of the Court to encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial disputes and in exercise of its inherent powers can quash criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint and Section 320 of the Code does not limit or affect the powers under Section 482 of the Code.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. The matter arises out of matrimonial dispute.

In view of the settlement having taken place, no purpose will be served in continuing the criminal proceeding initiated against 2003(4) SCC 675 NC:
2025:KHC:9125 the petitioners.
Hence, to meet the ends of justice, the criminal proceeding pending against the petitioners is liable to be quashed.
10. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is allowed.
The entire proceeding arising out of Crime No.505/2021 registered in Madanayakanahally Police Station, Bengaluru District is hereby quashed.
11. I.A.No.1/2023 does not survive for consideration and the same is disposed of.
